Q1.5 Model the Nozzle

We model the nozzle using the electrical circuit in Fig. 3 and a lumped
thermal model. The input is the controllable nozzle voltage u_n.

Variables and parameters :

u_n    Input voltage [V]
V_c    Voltage across the capacitor and resistor [V]
i_n    Current through the inductor [A]
i_C    Capacitor current [A]
i_R    Resistor current [A]
T_n    Nozzle temperature [K]
T_e    Environmental temperature [K]
L_n    Inductance [H]
C_n    Capacitance [F]
R_n    Electrical resistance [ohm]
C_t,n  Nozzle thermal capacity [J/K]
R_t,n  Equivalent nozzle thermal resistance [K/W]


1. Thermal model
The resistor and the capacitor are in parallel, so the resistor voltage
is equal to V_c. Electrical power dissipated in the resistor is

P_in = V_c^2 / R_n

The thermal energy stored in the nozzle changes at the rate

P_stored = C_t,n * dT_n/dt

The heat loss to the environment (including the filament, represented
by an equivalent thermal resistance) is

P_out = (T_n - T_e) / R_t,n

From the energy balance,

P_stored = P_in - P_out

C_t,n * dT_n/dt = V_c^2/R_n - (T_n - T_e)/R_t,n

Therefore,

dT_n/dt = V_c^2/(C_t,n * R_n) - (T_n - T_e)/(C_t,n * R_t,n)


2. Electrical model

Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL) for the inductor and parallel branch:

u_n = V_L + V_c
V_L = L_n * di_n/dt

Therefore,

di_n/dt = (u_n - V_c)/L_n

Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL) at the parallel branch:

i_n = i_C + i_R

i_C = C_n * dV_c/dt
i_R = V_c/R_n

Therefore,

i_n = C_n * dV_c/dt + V_c/R_n

dV_c/dt = i_n/C_n - V_c/(C_n * R_n)


3. State-space description

We choose the state vector

x_n = [T_n, V_c, i_n]^T

and the input u_n. The state derivative is

dx_n/dt = [dT_n/dt, dV_c/dt, di_n/dt]^T

The resulting state-space model is

dx_n/dt = f_n(x_n, u_n),

with

f_n(x_n, u_n) = [
    V_c^2/(C_t,n * R_n) - (T_n - T_e)/(C_t,n * R_t,n),
    i_n/C_n - V_c/(C_n * R_n),
    (u_n - V_c)/L_n
]^T

The model is nonlinear because the thermal equation contains V_c^2.
